# r3v3rs3

> A reverse proxy server with a built-in WebUI for TCP, UDP, TLS, HTTP, WebSocket and HTTP/3, and a deployment platform that runs your apps behind it, written in Rust. It is a fork of Taxy.

r3v3rs3 runs as a single binary. You configure it in a browser, not in a configuration file: every port, proxy, certificate and account is a form in the WebUI, and the same operations are available over an admin API. It can also build its proxies from Docker labels or etcd keys.

The deployment platform runs apps as containers on the Docker Engine of the server or of a remote server with the r3v3rs3 agent. An app comes from a registry image, from a Git repository with its Dockerfile, or from the Docker Compose file of a Git repository. A deployment is blue-green, and r3v3rs3 routes the domains of the apps itself. Git provider connections (a GitHub App, or an OAuth app for GitLab and Gitea) list the repositories, clone private ones and install the push webhook that starts a deployment.

The documentation is published in English at the root and in Turkish under `/tr/`. Every page listed below has a Turkish translation at the same path with the `/tr/` prefix. This file carries the extended descriptions of every page; the short index lives at [llms.txt](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/llms.txt).

## Reference

- [Overview](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/): the feature list of the current release, grouped into proxying, security and traffic control, certificates, operations and the deployment platform, with the installation commands.
- [Configuration](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/configuration/): every setting of the server with its default value: the six port types (HTTP, HTTPS, HTTP/3 over QUIC, TCP, TCP over TLS, UDP), the routing order, path rewrite, redirect rules, fixed responses, load balancing and health checks, the circuit breaker, sticky sessions, retries, traffic mirroring, timeouts, the request body limit, the client IP resolution behind CDNs, the IP filter, the rate limit, the four authentication methods, access lists, header rules with their variables, compression, the HTTP cache, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 limits, certificates and ACME with all DNS-01 providers, worker processes, the zero-downtime and in-panel upgrades, the Prometheus metrics, the MCP server, the admin API and the log files.
- [Accounts](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/accounts/): the `admin`, `editor` and `viewer` roles, what each permission covers, the per-account proxy lists, TOTP, the session and login-attempt limits, and where the accounts are stored.
- [Service Discovery](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/discovery/): the Docker label keys, the etcd settings, the label grammar (types, numbered lists, defaults), the ACME integration of discovered proxies and the issue reporting.
- [Deployment Platform](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/platform/): image, Git and Compose apps, blue-green deployments with health checks and rollback, encrypted environment variables, the Git provider connections (a private GitHub App, OAuth apps for GitLab and Gitea), the verified push webhooks, the agent targets with their mTLS enrollment and the notification events.
- [Release Verification](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/release-verification/): how to verify a downloaded release binary against its sha256 digest and signature.
- [Development](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/development/): the toolchain requirements and the commands that build, test, lint and release the workspace.

## Tutorials

- [Installing on a Linux Server](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/tutorials/install-linux/): run install.sh, what it asks and what it writes, the systemd unit, the file locations, the upgrade, the removal and the agent enrollment.
- [Getting Started](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/tutorials/getting-started/): from the first admin account to the first working proxy in five steps, with the HTTPS and ACME follow-up.
- [Proxies from Docker](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/tutorials/docker-discovery/): a working Compose stack where containers define their own proxies with `r3v3rs3.` labels, scale to replicas, and get certificates from an ACME entry by label.
- [HTTPS with a Wildcard Certificate](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/tutorials/https-certificates/): order a wildcard certificate with DNS-01, redirect HTTP to HTTPS, send HSTS as a header rule and add HTTP/3 with its `alt-svc` advertisement.
- [Protecting an Application](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/tutorials/protect-an-app/): an access list with an IP filter and Basic Auth, a rate limit with a burst, the four authentication methods compared, a route open for health checks, the client IP behind a CDN and the audit log.
- [Caching and Compression](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/tutorials/cache-and-compression/): turn on the response cache and compression, understand the TTL, the revalidation and the purge.
- [TCP and UDP Proxies](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/tutorials/tcp-and-udp/): publish PostgreSQL over TCP and a DNS server over UDP, add mutual TLS with self-signed certificates, encrypt the upstream connection and drain a server.
- [Load Balancing and Health Checks](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/tutorials/load-balancing/): the four policies, weights, active and passive checks, retries, sticky sessions, draining a server, the circuit breaker, traffic mirroring and WebSocket plus gRPC with h2c.
- [Driving r3v3rs3 from a Script](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/tutorials/admin-api/): sign in to the admin API, read the OpenAPI document, create a port and a proxy, purge a cache and give a deploy job its own account.
- [Proxies from etcd](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/tutorials/etcd-discovery/): define proxies through etcd keys, follow the changes of the keys and read the issue reports.
- [Accounts for a Team](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/tutorials/team-accounts/): give each person a role and a proxy list, turn on TOTP, protect an application with the same panel accounts and read who changed what.
- [Single Sign-On with Forward Auth](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/tutorials/forward-auth/): put oauth2-proxy in front of an application, publish its endpoints, forward the user headers and leave the health check route open.
- [Migrating from nginx or Traefik](https://r3v3rs3.keremgok.tr/tutorials/migrate/): translate the directives and labels, run both proxies side by side, compare the responses and cut the traffic over without downtime.

## Source and packages

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/KilimcininKorOglu/r3v3rs3): the source, the issue tracker and the release archives.
- [crates.io: r3v3rs3](https://crates.io/crates/r3v3rs3): the server binary package; it ships the built WebUI.
- [crates.io: r3v3rs3-api](https://crates.io/crates/r3v3rs3-api): the shared API types and validation.
- [docs.rs: r3v3rs3-api](https://docs.rs/r3v3rs3-api): the rustdoc reference of the API types.
- [Changelog](https://github.com/KilimcininKorOglu/r3v3rs3/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): the notable changes of every release in Keep a Changelog format.
